canvas-01-1.description: This part of printed sheet 1 shows Chester Station, which the sheet places about one mile north of the Chester post office, at 50 feet to an inch. It is the terminus of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad's Chester Branch. Hillside Road, also labelled Railroad Avenue, runs along the left edge, and Factory Street leaves it eastward across the middle of the part. North of Factory Street, block 30 holds the railroad yard: two tracks ending near Hillside Road, a passenger depot, a freight house with a platform, a locomotive house reached through a turntable, and a coal bin. Along the south track H. W. Cyphers' coal and lumber yard has a long coal shed, a lumber shed, a storage shed, and an office with scales. South of Factory Street, block 31 holds the brick works of William Sturzenegger's embroidery manufactory (factories 1 and 2, with an office and a coal bin; steam heat, power by hand, electric light) and a frame dwelling. On the west side of Hillside Road stands the Anthracite Hotel with its bar, and a small ice house and stable at the very edge of the sheet. The rest of the part is vacant fields. A large compass rose is drawn at the left, but it points about 17 degrees away from north as given by the streets; the part was placed from the streets.
notes: Factory is now Oakdale Road; Hillside Road keeps its name.
The Chester Branch of the D.L. & W. R.R. was abandoned in the 1930s; OpenStreetMap shows its former line ending just north of Hillside Road / Oakdale Road.

Placed from a single junction (Hillside Road / Oakdale Road) with the scale of sheets 2 and 3 and the rotation measured from the drawn streets; the drawn compass rose disagrees with the streets by about 17 degrees.

Printed sheet 1 (title, specials index, key and key map, which are left out of every mask). Scale 50 ft to an inch. Three map parts: part 1 Chester Station on the D.L.&W.R.R. Chester Branch, about 1 mile north of the village (Hillside Road / Factory Street, now Oakdale Road; north arrow on the sheet disagrees with the streets by about 17 degrees, placed from the streets); part 2 Main Street, North Avenue, Depot Street and Washington Turnpike at the east end of the village (now Main Street / North Road / Oakdale Road; Washington Turnpike survives as the north end of Fairmount Avenue, cut off from Main); part 3 Hillside Road west of the Public Square with the 1st Congregational Church, chapel and cemetery (not placed). Parts 1 and 2 each have one street junction and are anchored on it.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Hillside Road (Railroad Avenue) west of the Public Square: 1st Congregational Church, chapel, cemetery, blocks 1 and 6 (no street junction drawn (Hedges Road, which now meets Hillside Road here, is not drawn) and no feature shared with sheets 2 or 3; the part is not adjacent to them ('No exposure' edge), so its position along Hillside Road is uncertain by tens of metres; needs a surviving boundary (church lot or cemetery) matched to modern parcels or aerial imagery, then step 6b).

canvas-01-2.description: This part of printed sheet 1 shows the east end of Chester village at 50 feet to an inch, with north to the upper left. Depot Street crosses the top of the part, North Avenue leaves it northward, and below it Main Street runs off to the lower left while the Washington Turnpike runs down the middle, parallel to Main. The meeting of these four roads is drawn as a broad open junction. North of Depot Street, block 25 holds three frame dwellings and a brick dwelling, and block 26 the Flag Staff Inn, a frame hotel with a bar, heated by stoves and lit by acetylene gas, with stables and outbuildings behind it. South of Depot Street, the narrow block 28 between Main and the Washington Turnpike holds a dwelling, a blacksmith shop and small sheds, and block 29 west of Main is vacant. Block 27, east of the turnpike, has a vacant store and a few dwellings and sheds. The edges are marked as having no exposure. The upper right of the printed sheet, outside this part, carries the title cartouche, the specials index, the key and a small key map of the village with a location map of New Jersey.
notes: Main is now Main Street, North Avenue is North Road, Depot west of the junction is Oakdale Road and Depot east of it is Main Street.
Washington Turnpike survives as the north end of Fairmount Avenue, which no longer reaches Main Street.
Placed from a single junction (Main Street / North Road / Oakdale Road) with the scale of sheets 2 and 3 and the rotation measured from the drawn streets.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northern half of the village centre of Chester, Morris County, in October 1912, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left of the page. Main Street runs up the left half of the sheet from the Public Square to Church Street; it is drawn 65 to 88 feet wide. Budd Avenue leaves the square diagonally to the north-east and is crossed by Orange and Cherry Streets, and Grove Street runs from the square along the lower edge to Mud Street. West of Main lies block 1, with a row of frame stores and halls facing the square: the brick Chester House hotel with bar and hall, a wagon repository with a hall on the upper floors, a seed store, a general hall with a doctor's office, and an auto house. Further north on that side stand Janes' M.E. Church and scattered dwellings, with vacant ground behind. East of Main, block 2 holds a general store, storage buildings, an ice house, a livery stable and dwellings, and at its north end the Presbyterian Church with its tower and a separate chapel. Between Budd Avenue and Grove Street the District Public School No. 55 stands in a large lot with a wood shed and outbuildings. Blocks 3, 4 and 5 along Orange and Cherry Streets are lightly built with frame dwellings, chicken houses and stables. Nearly every building is frame. The lower edge repeats part of the block south of Grove Street that sheet 3 draws in full.
notes: Mud Street is now Maple Avenue.
Main Street north-east of the Public Square keeps its name; south-west of the square the modern name in OpenStreetMap is Main Street (Old Rt. 24).
Hillside Road is labelled with its other name, Railroad Avenue, in brackets.
Main Street is drawn 88 ft wide at Church Street and 65 ft at the Public Square, much wider than today's carriageway; Main / Church was hand-picked.

Scale 50 ft to an inch. Main Street north-east of the Public Square to Church Street, Budd Avenue, Orange, Cherry and Grove Streets, Mud Street (now Maple Avenue). One part. Main drawn 65 to 88 ft wide.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the southern half of the village centre of Chester, Morris County, in October 1912, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Main Street runs down the sheet from the Public Square, where Hillside Road (Railroad Avenue) leaves to the west, past Grove, Warren, Perry and Seminary Streets; Mud Street runs parallel to Main along the right side. The west side of Main, block 6, is the main commercial frontage: a feed, kerosene and storage building, a dry goods, grocery and hardware store, drugs and paints with notions and printing, confectionery and tobacco, ice cream, barber and billiards, a grocery, a tin shop with stoves and kerosene, and dwellings behind. On the east side, block 7 between Grove and Warren holds the post office, a meat market, an ice house and dwellings; block 8 between Warren and Perry has a cobbler, a blacksmith, a barber, a grocery, wagon houses, sheds, and the Chester Garage with a buried gasoline tank; block 11 below Perry has the Centennial Building with feed, flour and grain and a hardware store. Across Mud Street the Town Hall, which also houses a motion picture theatre, stands at the corner of Grove. Blocks 9, 10 and 12 at the right and bottom edges are only partly drawn, with vacant land beyond. Buildings are almost all frame; the Chester Garage and a small building behind block 6 are coloured as stone or iron. The top edge repeats the corner of the Chester House hotel that sheet 2 draws in full.
notes: Main south-west of the Public Square is Main Street (Old Rt. 24) in OpenStreetMap.
Mud is now Maple Avenue.
Main is drawn 95 ft wide between the square and Warren and 70 ft below it; Main / Warren was hand-picked because the detector paired the wrong lines there.
The Town Hall is labelled as a motion picture theatre as well.

Scale 50 ft to an inch. Main Street (now Main Street (Old Rt. 24)) south-west of the Public Square, Grove, Warren, Perry and Seminary, Mud Street (now Maple Avenue), Hillside Road (Railroad Avenue). One part.
